deep.reconstruction:
Context. Folios 175r–176r are drafts of Riemann's Dirichlet-principle argument and of the covering letter to the editor of Crelle's Journal (Borchardt) for the 1857 Abelian-functions papers. The previous page sets up a Dirichlet-type integral Omega with an admissible class of comparison functions. The next page sets up Omega(alpha) = ∫_T [(alpha_x - beta_y)^2 + (alpha_y + beta_x)^2] dT for alpha with prescribed boundary values, together with the quadratic expansion and uniqueness argument.

(1) End of the admissible-class definition (top line). The comparison class (on the previous page, 'Erste Klasse') consists of all functions alpha - beta. Here beta is continuous together with all its first derivatives and vanishes on the boundary of T. Admissible functions therefore have the boundary values of alpha.

(2) First worry: the minimum may not be attained (lines 2-4, partly struck). Riemann writes that it is 'of course still possible' that Omega takes arbitrarily small values (I read this as: approaches its lower bound) as beta approaches a discontinuous function gamma. Such a gamma would be discontinuous along a line yet be such that ∫_T (gamma_x^2 + gamma_y^2) dT stays finite. The text breaks off.

(3) Conjugate-function construction (middle block). Let u be the minimizer. By the next page, the first variation vanishes:
∫[(u_x - beta_y) sigma_x + (u_y + beta_x) sigma_y] dT = 0 for all sigma vanishing on the boundary.
Hence d/dx(u_x - beta_y) + d/dy(u_y + beta_x) = 0, i.e. Laplacian(u) = 0. Riemann writes the line integral
∫ (v_x + u_y) dx + (v_y - u_x) dy, with v = beta.
Its closedness condition is d/dy(beta_x + u_y) - d/dx(beta_y - u_x) = u_xx + u_yy = 0, which is exactly the Euler-Lagrange equation. So 'the integral taken around the whole boundary of any part of T is = 0.'
- If T is multiply connected, cut it by Querschnitte (cross-cuts) into a simply connected T*.
- In T*, V(x,y) = ∫ (beta_x + u_y) dx + (beta_y - u_x) dy is single-valued and not discontinuous along any line in the interior. It jumps by constants (the periods) across the cuts.
- Then (beta - V)_x = -u_y and (beta - V)_y = u_x.
- So W = u + i(beta - V) satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann equations, which Riemann writes as i dW/dx = dW/dy. W is thus an analytic function of x+iy in T*. This is the step 'existence of a complex function with prescribed real-part data' used in the published paper.

(4) Second, cleaner draft of the worry (lower block). 'It was asserted above that Omega(alpha - beta), when all continuous functions are substituted for beta, must necessarily attain a minimum for one of these functions. But it is also possible that Omega becomes arbitrarily small [approaches its infimum] the more beta approaches a discontinuous function gamma, so that the minimum is not attained even for this discontinuous function.' The sentence is not completed and no remedy is given.

(5) Letter draft (bottom). Riemann asks permission to 'send ahead the general assumptions and foundations of these investigations.' Of the three divisions (Abtheilungen) of the essay, the first contains the foundations for the theory of integrals of complete (two-term) differentials. This corresponds to the preliminary notes in Crelle 54 (1857) preceding 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen', notably 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs für die Theorie der Integrale von zweigliedrigen vollständigen Differentialen'.
errors: The tacit inference 'Omega is finite and never negative, hence some admissible function gives a minimum' is unjustified: the infimum need not be attained in the admissible class. This is Weierstrass's 1870 objection. On this page Riemann himself raises precisely this possibility, but he does not resolve it.
The phrase 'beliebig klein' should be read as 'arbitrarily close to its lower bound'. Taken literally (Omega -> 0) it would mean the infimum is 0, which is not the general concern.

The specific scenario (a limit function discontinuous along a line with finite Dirichlet integral) is impossible: a jump across a curve forces infinite Dirichlet energy, as Riemann himself notes on the previous page. The modern reason the infimum is attained in a suitable class is weak lower semicontinuity and compactness in W^{1,2}, which were unavailable to Riemann.

The closedness of the differential (beta_x+u_y)dx+(beta_y-u_x)dy requires only Laplacian(u)=0. Deriving this from the weak (integrated) Euler-Lagrange equation for a merely finite-energy u (Weyl's lemma) is assumed without proof.
Notational slips: 'beta - v = v' (lowercase/uppercase confusion between beta-V and nu), and 'i du/dx = dv/dy' presumably meant i dW/dx = dW/dy.

results.what: Admissible class for the Dirichlet-type minimum problem: alpha - beta, with beta C^1 and vanishing on the boundary (fixed boundary values)
results.modern_name: Dirichlet problem via variational (Dirichlet) principle, admissible class with fixed boundary data
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Thomson (1847), Dirichlet (lectures); named Dirichlet principle by Riemann 1851/1857

results.what: Explicit doubt that the infimum of the Dirichlet integral is attained: minimizing sequences might tend to a discontinuous function outside the class
results.modern_name: Non-attainment of the infimum / existence gap in Dirichlet's principle (Weierstrass's objection); direct method of the calculus of variations
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (1870 critique), resolved by Hilbert (1900/1904), later Sobolev-space methods

results.what: From the vanishing first variation, the differential (beta_x+u_y)dx+(beta_y-u_x)dy is closed; on a simply connected T* obtained by cross-cuts it integrates to V, and W = u + i(beta - V) is analytic (Cauchy-Riemann)
results.modern_name: Construction of the harmonic conjugate / periods across cuts on a Riemann surface

results.what: Plan of the 1857 publication in three preliminary divisions, the first being foundations for integrals of complete differentials

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is a draft of known material from the 1857 Abelian-functions paper: the admissible class, the closed differential, cutting into T*, and the analytic function u+i(beta-V). The notable item is Riemann's own explicit, twice-drafted worry that the infimum might not be attained because minimizing functions could approach a discontinuous limit. This is essentially the gap Weierstrass made famous in 1870, and it was suppressed in the published text. Historians have speculated about Riemann's awareness, and some Nachlass work may already mention it. I am unsure whether this passage is documented, so I rate it moderately notable rather than major. He offers no counterexample and no resolution.

checkable.asserts: Closedness defect of (b_x+u_y)dx+(b_y-u_x)dy equals Laplacian(u) (result 0), so the form is closed iff u is harmonic.
The Euler-Lagrange expression of Omega(alpha)=∫((a_x-b_y)^2+(a_y+b_x)^2)dT at a=u reduces to Laplacian(u): beta drops out (result 0).

checkable.asserts: For harmonic u and arbitrary b, V exists with the given differential, and W=u+i(b-V) satisfies Cauchy-Riemann (all entries 0).

Integrand of the Dirichlet integral of the previous page's example (-log r)^e near r=0 is 2*pi*e^2*(-log r)^(2e-2)/r. Substituting t=-log r gives ∫ t^(2e-2) dt over t>t0, which converges at infinity iff e<1/2 (finite energy, unbounded function).

transcription_corrections: 'i ∂u/∂x = ∂v/∂y' is most likely 'i ∂W/∂x = ∂W/∂y' (Cauchy-Riemann for W = u+(β−V)i).

In the formula line, 'β−v = v   V=β−v' should probably read something like '... − V = ν, V = β − ν' (the line-integral value is denoted by V). The image shows the integral followed by '− V = v' and then 'V = β − v'. Lowercase v/ν versus V is uncertain.
The integrand of the line integral is (∂v/∂x + ∂u/∂y)dx + (∂v/∂y − ∂u/∂x)dy, with v playing the role of β. This is consistent with the next page's Euler-Lagrange expression.

'{+Kriterien+}' in the last line is uncertain; it may be 'Prinzipien' or similar. The phrase is 'die Grundlagen für die Lehre ... der Integrale ... vollständiger Differentiale', matching the title of the published analysis-situs note.
Line 1 begins with an inserted word (possibly 'Ihr'/'die') above 'alle Functionen von der Form α−β'. The insertion above 'stetige' reads 'mit allen ihren ersten [Derivirten]'.
